Dates or anniversaries connected to the event

Memory.value: My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish

vignette: Kamran's life was forever altered on a sweltering summer evening three years ago. He had just finished a long day of tending to his farm, and was walking home from the fields when he was suddenly ambushed by a group of strangers. They beat him mercilessly, leaving him for dead in a ditch. Kamran's memories of that night are fragmented and disjointed – flashes of fists flying, the sound of footsteps receding into the distance, the feeling of his head cracking against the ground. As he slowly came to, Kamran was consumed by a sense of confusion and disorientation. His memories of the event feel alien to him, as if they belong to someone else entirely. When he tries to recount what happened, he becomes overwhelmed and lost for words, unable to piece together the events of that fateful night. In the aftermath of the assault, Kamran began to notice strange somatic sensations – his heart racing or pounding in response to seemingly innocuous stimuli. The smell of sweat or body odor would transport him back to that ditch, where he would relive the terror and helplessness. He became hypervigilant, constantly on the lookout for potential threats, convinced that people acting suspiciously were lurking around every corner. Kamran's wife, Fatima, noticed a change in his behavior – he would become withdrawn and irritable at odd moments, or suddenly throw himself into his work with an intensity that left him exhausted. He couldn't shake the feeling of vulnerability, the sense that he was always looking over his shoulder, waiting for the next attack. As the anniversaries of the assault approached, Kamran found himself becoming increasingly anxious and withdrawn. He would ruminate about how to get even with his assailants, fantasizing about revenge scenarios that left him feeling momentarily empowered but ultimately empty. To cope with these dark impulses, he threw himself into his work, taking on extra tasks and responsibilities to keep his mind occupied. But the avoidance behaviors came at a cost – Kamran's relationships with Fatima and their children began to suffer. They would try to talk to him about his feelings, but he would shut down, unable to articulate the turmoil brewing inside. He became isolated, spending long hours alone in the fields or the barn, lost in thought. As the months turned into years, Kamran's farm began to suffer as well. Crops went untended, equipment fell into disrepair, and the once-thriving business began to falter. Fatima tried to step in, but Kamran pushed her away, convinced that he was the only one who could keep everything together. It wasn't until a recent confrontation with his son, Amir, that Kamran realized he needed help. Amir had been trying to talk to him about his own struggles in school, but Kamran became so overwhelmed by his own emotions that he lashed out at the boy, sending him running from the room in tears. In that moment, Kamran saw himself through Fatima's eyes – a shadow of the man he once was, consumed by anger and fear. As he sat on the couch, staring blankly into space, Kamran knew he couldn't keep going like this. He made an appointment with a therapist, hoping to find some way to quiet the demons that haunted him, to piece together the fragments of his memories and reclaim his life from the trauma that had taken hold.
